names: 'The first sync starts with the next background job. It loads the chat history.')

lines: One chunk holds at least 90.0 % of a page, so the browser fetches practically the whole page before it shows anything:
chat_archive-main.mjs: 1 file, 2,007,206 B, of which chat_archive-main.mjs is 2,007,206 B (100.0 %).
chat_archive-settings.mjs: 1 file, 1,791,697 B, of which chat_archive-settings.mjs is 1,791,697 B (100.0 %).

Code splitting puts what the first paint does not need behind a dynamic import, and then the browser fetches it when the code asks. Which part of a page that is does not follow from the build output; the source decides it.
1 package is imported by their root in src, so the whole barrel is reachable and the bundler keeps whatever it cannot prove unused:

@nextcloud/vue: 235,189 B in 52 modules, 11.7 % of the static path of chat_archive-main.mjs, imported by its root in 10 files: App.vue (NcActionCaption, NcActionCheckbox, NcActionRadio, ...), components/CallList.vue (NcButton, NcEmptyContent, NcSelect, ...), and 8 more.
Importing the module that is used instead of the package root lets the bundler drop the rest of the barrel.
ncmake's lint-vue-imports workflow gates exactly this specifier for @nextcloud/vue, so this finding is that red check with a byte figure attached.

2 components of @nextcloud/vue are delivered although no file in src names them, no other dependency names them and no component named by either imports them: 142,474 B, 8.0 % of the static path of chat_archive-settings.mjs, next to 2 components the source names, 1 that other dependencies name.
NcIconToggleSwitch 142,449 B, NcReferenceWidget 25 B.
These arrive through the root import: under a barrel the whole component set is reachable, so the bundler must keep it. Per-component imports leave it free to drop what the app never names.
Built with: vite.config.js, package.json declares @nextcloud/vite-config ^2.5.0 (locked 2.5.4), vite ^7.3.6 (locked 7.3.6).
@nextcloud/vue ^9.0.0 declared.
Written against: vue 3.5.42, 16 delivered packages.
Other delivered libraries: 92, axios 1.20.0, mdast-util-to-hast 13.2.1, focus-trap 8.2.2, @nextcloud/logger 3.0.3, mdast-util-from-markdown 2.0.3, semver 7.8.5, and 86 more.
Packages and versions are those the .license files beside the chunks name, since the source maps miss packages through the toolchain defect named here.

Known toolchain defect: vite-plugin-css-injected-by-js 4.0.1 in package-lock.json, where the CSS is injected by JavaScript, puts the code that injects the CSS in front of the chunk without shifting its source map, so the map the bundler combines from it loses sources. Here the map of chat_archive-main.mjs names 35 of the 107 packages its .license file names, and 1 further chunk shows the same.
The app runs as built; only the map is short, so the frameworks and libraries are read from the .license files instead.
Fixed in vite-plugin-css-injected-by-js 5.0.0: https://github.com/marco-prontera/vite-plugin-css-injected-by-js/issues/155

Built in a copy with @nextcloud/vite-config 3.0.0-beta.1, vite 8.3.5 (vite-plugin-css-injected-by-js 5.0.3), the map of PublicAuthPrompt-hlHh0X0w.chunk.mjs names 6 of the 7 packages its .license file names: fixed.
Every delivered file in js carries a source map, so every byte can be charged to the package and the module it came from.
